findings.title: Second `self.downsize` silently replaces the first, breaking the 5-argument form
findings.body: The diff adds `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 is left in place. In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 5-argument form is gone. Any caller passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). The two overloads with the same name and different arities are a clear mistake. Either remove one, or keep a single method and update all callers.

findings.title: `optimize` no longer returns anything useful for callers that depended on the old signature
findings.body: `resize` and `downsize` previously passed width/height through `dimensions()`, which was removed. Any other caller outside this diff that calls `optimize` or `downsize` with width and height, or relies on the removed `dimensions` helper, will break. The PR does not show a search of all call sites to confirm this is safe.

findings.title: Size check uses a stale `tempfile.size` after the file is rewritten in place
findings.body: The loop re-reads `tempfile.size` on a Tempfile object whose descriptor was opened before `OptimizedImage.downsize` rewrote `tempfile.path` via an external process and ImageOptim. Depending on whether the rewrite replaces the inode, `File#size` on the open handle can return the old size. The loop may then run all 5 attempts needlessly, or stop incorrectly. The size should be read from the path (for example `File.size(tempfile.path)`) and the handle reopened or flushed.

findings.title: Failed downsizes are retried silently and oversize images are still accepted
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false on failure (its result is ignored here), so a failing convert is retried up to 5 times on the same input with no effect. If the image is still above `max_image_size_kb` after the loop, nothing is raised or reported; the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the oversize file. The user gets no clear error and the limit the admin configured is not enforced consistently.

findings.title: Remote URL downloads are no longer bounded by the admin size setting
findings.body: The download limit for API URL uploads was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hard-coded `10.megabytes`. Admins who set a lower limit now get downloads of up to 10MB for any file type, and the download is not checked against the setting before being written to disk. This is a behavior change that the PR does not justify or make configurable.

findings.title: Client-side size check ignores per-type site settings and hard-codes 10MB
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. It now always uses 10MB. Admin limits for attachments and images are ignored in the browser, and the hard-coded 10MB check also blocks any image above 10MB, which contradicts the server-side feature of accepting and downsizing large images. The client and server limits now disagree.

findings.title: 413 handler hard-codes the limit instead of using the configured setting
findings.body: The 413 case now displays a hard-coded 10 MB limit rather than `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. The message can be wrong for any site whose configured limit differs from 10MB.

findings.title: No tests added for the automatic downsizing path or the changed behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a new server-side loop that rewrites uploaded files, changes `OptimizedImage` method signatures, and changes size limits on both client and server. None of these changes have specs covering the downsize loop, the attempt limit, the failure path, the overload issue, or the size checks. The description is just "Test 1", so the PR gives no rationale or verification steps.
